* [4056](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/4056): Fix accidentally dropping filters in complex joins
filter-branch creates a new database for each commit it replays and never closed them, so their sequence trackers could still be reading the store when dolt closed it. That panic made filter-branch.bats fail intermittently. The rebased engine now closes the databases it owns, and filter-branch closes the engine. Adds a unit regression test.

Migration from v5: v5's Keyv also prefixed every key with `<namespace>:`, so the setting depends on the adapter. A default v5 `@keyv/redis` setup stored `keyv::keyv:foo`, which v6 reads with `new Keyv(new KeyvRedis(uri, { namespaceSeparator: '::keyv:' }), { namespace: 'keyv' })`. If you used `createKeyv()`, set only the same `namespace`. For other adapters, see [The Default `keyv` Namespace Was Removed](https://keyv.org/docs/migration/v5-to-v6/#the-default-keyv-namespace-was-removed).

A PostgreSQL worker with `CONN_MAX_AGE = 0` and no `OPTIONS["pool"]` now logs one warning at start, because every task opens a new database connection. Set `CONN_MAX_AGE = 600`, or set `OPTIONS["pool"]` and leave `CONN_MAX_AGE` at 0. "Retaining worker connections" in the production guide lists both settings and the pool size to use.
The benchmarks page now reports django-ox 1.9.0 against django-tasks-db 0.13.0 at the same connection settings: 1.4 to 1.7 times the tasks per second with pooled or persistent c

- Existing django-ox users need no database migration for this upgrade.
- Before upgrading, psycopg2 and mysqlclient users must run the boundary

- With psycopg_pool 3.3.0 or later, PostgreSQL pool recovery no longer runs statements on idle connections. In django-ox 1.5.0 through 1.7.0, the recovery sweep could wait indefinitely for an idle connection that stayed open without answering. Recovery now drains the pool only when the driver reports a connection as lost. Idle connections are closed without testing them. Checked-out connections are closed and replaced when returned. A failed attempt with no reported connection loss leaves the pool alone.
